title: The Third Regression
brief: For the third release in a row, the Meridian Digital reporting service has shipped a regression in the export feature. Each time the defect was fixed quickly. Problem record PRB-40 says "cause: developer oversight". You have 12 visit points to interview the team and reach a system cause.

actions.label: Defect data for the last 3 releases
General condition of the area
actions.note: Nothing of note for the purpose of this visit.

actions.label: Developer: how export code is changed
Developer: what tests run before merge
Test lead: who owns export tests
A staff member: anything else to mention
actions.note: The staff member has nothing further to add on this topic.

actions.note: The older records show nothing relevant to this visit.

actions.label: Notices and signs in the area
actions.note: The notices are current and not relevant to this visit.

evidence.text: PRB-40 lists "developer oversight" as the cause and "be more careful" as the action. It was closed after release 9 with no check; regressions recurred in releases 10 and 11.
evidence.whyItMatters: Corrective action must find and remove the cause and confirm the action worked. Naming a person stops the analysis.
evidence.missedExplanation: Read the cause and the check in every closed problem record.

evidence.text: Defect data: all 3 regressions were in the CSV export path, each after a change to the shared formatting module.
evidence.whyItMatters: The data points to a pattern. Analyzing it is the first step toward a system cause.
evidence.missedExplanation: Look for what the recurrences have in common.

evidence.text: Developer: "Export uses the shared formatter. We change the formatter for other features too." The developer raises the concern openly.
evidence.whyItMatters: The developer gives a useful lead without blame.
evidence.falseFindingNote: The developer is describing the system, not making an error.

evidence.text: Developer: "Before merge only unit tests for the changed module run. Export tests run nightly, after merge." Pipeline stage list confirms this in stage 2.
evidence.whyItMatters: Monitoring must happen at stages that prevent nonconforming output from moving on. Running export tests after merge lets regressions reach the release.
evidence.missedExplanation: Ask which tests run before a change is merged.

evidence.text: Test lead: "Nobody owns the export tests since the last reorganization in month 4. Failures in the nightly run are not assigned."
evidence.whyItMatters: Responsibilities for quality-relevant activities must be assigned and understood.
evidence.missedExplanation: Ask who owns each test suite and its failures.

evidence.text: Export test coverage: 2 of 9 export formats have automated tests. Requirement EXP-3 lists all 9.
evidence.missedExplanation: Compare requirement lists with test lists.

evidence.text: Pipeline history: the export test stage was moved from pre-merge to nightly in change PL-19 to cut build time; no review of the effect is recorded.
evidence.whyItMatters: This change explains when the problem began. A review of its effect is the missing step; recording it is an improvement opportunity.
evidence.missedExplanation: Ask what changed in the pipeline and when.

evidence.text: Product owner: export requirements are written with acceptance criteria for each format; requirement EXP-3 is current.
evidence.falseFindingNote: The requirements are clear. The gap is in verification.

evidence.text: Retrospective notes record the regressions and suggest "more tests" but no owner was assigned.
evidence.whyItMatters: The team reflects on problems; the notes are honest and useful.
evidence.falseFindingNote: Retrospectives are working as a discussion forum. Conforming.

evidence.text: The onboarding checklist does not mention the shared formatter or its dependents; 2 of the 3 regressions were made by developers in their first 3 months.
evidence.whyItMatters: Competence for working on shared modules could be improved through onboarding.
evidence.missedExplanation: Check what new staff are taught about shared code.

evidence.text: Build duration chart shows builds take 14 minutes on average.
evidence.whyItMatters: Build time explains a past decision but is not itself a nonconformity.
evidence.falseFindingNote: Build time is context. It is not a breach.

evidence.text: Team rota shows 2 developers on leave during release 11.
evidence.whyItMatters: Normal leave is not a cause by itself; cover was arranged.
evidence.falseFindingNote: Leave was covered. Do not build a cause from it.

decisions.prompt: Which statement best describes the system cause?
options: Export tests were moved after merge, have no owner, and cover only 2 of 9 formats, so changes to the shared formatter reach release unverified
The release cadence is too fast
The formatting module is badly written
decisions.rationale: The evidence shows conditions that would let anyone's change through: test timing, ownership, and coverage.

containment: Run the full export tests before the next release and hold it until they pass
correction: Fix the current export regression and add tests for the failing format
cause: Export tests run after merge, have no owner, and cover only 2 of 9 formats
corrective: Restore export tests to pre-merge, assign an owner, extend coverage to all 9 formats, and review pipeline changes for effect
Reopen PRB-40 with the system cause
effectiveness: Track export regressions for the next six releases, target zero

debriefText.found: You reached the system: test timing, ownership, and coverage.
debriefText.missed: When a defect recurs, look for what changed in the process and who owns the check.
debriefText.falseFinding: Build time and staff leave are context, not causes.
